kept.q: A relay team of 4 runners is to be selected from 7 athletes at a Lagos state sports meet, and the selected runners must then be arranged in a running order. How many different running orders are possible?
kept.explanation: This requires an ordered selection, so we use permutation P(7,4) = 7!/(7-4)! = 7x6x5x4 = 840. Order matters because each runner has a specific position in the relay.
kept.pidgin: Because order dey important for relay, na permutation we go use. We go calculate P(7,4) = 7!/(7-4)! which give us 7x6x5x4 = 840.

kept.q: Find the number of ways a key chain with 6 distinct keys can be arranged on a circular ring, given that arrangements that are mirror images (flips) of each other are considered the same.
kept.explanation: Circular arrangements of 6 distinct objects give (6-1)! = 120 ways. Since a ring can be flipped over, each arrangement is counted twice, so we divide by 2 to get 60.
kept.pidgin: For circular arrangement, we dey use (6-1)! = 120. Dem say make we divide by 2 because you fit flip the ring, so 120 divide by 2 na 60.

kept.q: How many different 4-letter codes can be formed from the letters of the word NIGER if letters may be repeated?
kept.explanation: NIGER has 5 distinct letters. Since repetition is allowed and each of the 4 positions can be filled in 5 ways, the total number of codes is 5^4 = 625.
kept.pidgin: NIGER get 5 letters and dem allow repetition. Since each of the 4 places get 5 ways, na 5^4 wey be 625.

kept.q: A debate team of 5 students is to be chosen from a group of 6 boys and 4 girls such that the team contains exactly 3 boys and 2 girls. In how many ways can this be done?
kept.explanation: Choose 3 boys from 6: C(6,3) = 20. Choose 2 girls from 4: C(4,2) = 6. Multiply the two results together: 20 x 6 = 120.
kept.pidgin: To choose 3 boys from 6 give C(6,3) = 20, and to choose 2 girls from 4 give C(4,2) = 6. When you multiply 20 and 6 together, you get 120.

kept.q: If P(n, 3) = 60, find the value of n.
kept.explanation: P(n,3) = n(n-1)(n-2) = 60. Testing n = 5 gives 5x4x3 = 60, which satisfies the equation. So n = 5.
kept.pidgin: P(n,3) mean say n(n-1)(n-2) = 60. If you check am well, 5x4x3 na 60, so n must be 5.

kept.q: A JAMB candidate must answer exactly 4 questions out of 6 questions in Section A and exactly 3 questions out of 5 questions in Section B. In how many ways can the candidate choose the questions to answer?
kept.explanation: Choosing 4 out of 6 in Section A gives C(6,4) = 15 ways, and choosing 3 out of 5 in Section B gives C(5,3) = 10 ways. Since both choices happen together, multiply: 15 x 10 = 150.
kept.pidgin: To choose 4 out of 6 for Section A na C(6,4) = 15, while 3 out of 5 for Section B na C(5,3) = 10. Multiply 15 and 10 together to get 150.

kept.q: In how many ways can 3 Mathematics books and 2 Physics books be arranged on a shelf so that the 2 Physics books are always kept next to each other?
kept.explanation: Treat the 2 Physics books as one single block, giving 4 items in total to arrange, which can be done in 4! = 24 ways. The 2 Physics books within the block can be arranged in 2! = 2 ways, giving 24 x 2 = 48.
kept.pidgin: Make we join the 2 Physics books together as one block, come arrange the 4 items as 4! = 24. Since the two Physics books fit rearrange themselves in 2! = 2 ways, 24 times 2 give us 48.

q.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word SUCCESS be arranged?
q.explanation: SUCCESS has 7 letters with S repeated 3 times and C repeated 2 times. Number of arrangements = 7!/(3!2!) = 5040/12 = 420.
